ceilingSources.residentMemoryBytes: rule: 2x the larger measured resident set (7598080 B over the recorded hosts), rounded up to a whole MiB; evidence runtime-budget.evidence/
ceilingSources.idleCpuPercent: rule: 1 percent absolute for an idle crate; measured at most 0.156 percent on the recorded hosts
ceilingSources.diskOpsPerSecond: rule: max(1, 2x measured) per second; Windows measured 0.0 (GetProcessIoCounters, all I/O including pipes); macOS exposes no per-process disk-operation counter
ceilingSources.wakeupsPerSecond: existing idle intent: src/lib.rs:1624 an_idle_service_wakes_its_threads_about_once_a_second_at_most; src/workers.rs:3-4 states the acceptor blocks in accept and liveness waits its whole 20-second period. One per second is the existing idle target, not a ceiling derived from the historical polling failure. Requires fresh native measurements at the declared 50-device scale.

status.note: The status call returns rightkit_child_process::ProcessUsage (resident and footprint bytes, cumulative CPU seconds, wake-up and disk-operation totals where the host reports them) beside the crate's own queue figures; the rates come from two calls (ProcessUsage::rates_since). Wake-ups are macOS only; disk operations are Windows and Linux only.

dataScale.description: 50 discovered devices; service idle for 30 seconds

measurements.command: rustright cargo test -p rightkit-send --profile dev --bench budget --jobs 12 -- 50 30

notes: Ceilings come from the stated sources. Historical macOS 0.1.0 evidence measured 15.3 wake-ups per second while the acceptor polled at 50 ms and liveness at 100 ms; those loops were replaced by blocking accept and a 20-second stop-aware wait. Historical evidence remains under runtime-budget.evidence/. The 1 per second idle target is unproven at 0.2.0: native-host measurement must include the declared 50-device scale and its liveness probes before publication.
